chunks: Section: As for the discussion regarding the birth of the Master of the Age (a.s) and its authenticity, there are two types: rational considerations and textual reports.

As for the rational part, it is that when his Imamate is established by the proofs we presented from the different categories, and every category is invalidated except the assertion of his Imamate, then his Imamate is established and we know the authenticity of his birth even if no report had come about it originally.
Also, what we proved regarding the Imams being twelve indicates the authenticity of his birth, because the number cannot exist except for something that is present/existent.
And what we proved regarding the Master of the Command having two occultations confirms that, because all of that is built upon the validity of his birth.

As for authenticating his birth through reports, we will mention in this book a portion of what has been narrated about it in summary and detail, and we will mention after that a group of reports from those who saw him and witnessed him, because completing everything narrated in this meaning would prolong the book.
ai.seo_question: How is the birth of Imam Mahdi (a.s) proven rationally and textually in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi structures the proof of Imam al-Mahdi’s (a.s.) birth by distinguishing between rational necessity (i'tibari), where the fixed number of twelve Imams and the reality of the two occultations logically demand a living heir, and textual evidence (ikhbari) from specific narrations. This dual approach underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on combining logical deduction with transmitted reports to establish the continuity of the Imamate. By linking the occultations directly to the prerequisite of birth, Tusi reinforces the theological coherence of the Mahdi's hidden presence.
